units.translation: and a lament for the newly plucked: if through tau, artitropois [newly turned], for those who have just turned from childhood and reached puberty; if through delta, artidropois [newly plucked], for those just being plucked. For those, he says, who are deflowered at the prime of life there will be lamentation, or, for those who are changing the path of captivity there will be tears.

Eustathius reads Opusc. p. 355, 28 ed. Tafel, for in autumn it is not only strange if, as the proverb says, a flower blooms, but also if, according to Aeschylus, a newly plucked fruit in its youth is harvested.
for in autumn it is not only strange if, as the proverb says, a flower blooms, but also if, according to Aeschylus, a newly plucked fruit in its youth is harvested
And the soft-moaning Persian women, longing to see the newly joined marriage of their husbands.
Schol. σύμφωνα καὶ ὑγιῶς συναρμοζόμενα ταῖς νεωστὶ συνθήκαις ἡμῶν [things in agreement and soundly fitted to our recent compacts].
So that these things may come together well-fitted.
And indeed this lord himself, the offspring of Oedipus, so that (sic I corrected for eis' artikollon) I may learn the well-fitted word of a messenger.
things in agreement and soundly fitted to our recent compacts
[Sept. 359 ἀρτιτρεφείς [newly born] erroneously for ἄρτι βρεφῶν [just of infants].]
sound of mind, in one's right mind
sound of mind, in one's right mind
But when he became sound of mind.
rich from ancient times, of ancient wealth
whose wealth is ancient (i.e. from ancestors), rich from olden times
Great is the gratitude of masters rich from ancient times.
Lamenting the grand and ancient-looking honor of your kindred.
τὸ ἀρχαῖον [the ancient time] in ancient times
Shame to the fatherland and to the ancient thrones.
To the gods they nailed these spoils in the houses throughout Greece, an ancient glory.
Lichens eating away the ancient nature.
You deceived the ancient goddesses with wine.
In the shepherd-haunted places of my ancient mother. My ancient race.
Perhaps I seem to you to be saying ancient things.
You seem to me to share in this land from ancient times.

In M there is the gloss λαῶν ἀρχόντων [of leaders of peoples], from which Robortellus wrote αρχελάων [leader of peoples], correctly, as it seems. Hermannus interprets ἀρχελείους [leaders of flocks] as leaders of flocks, whose note see.
And whom of the leaders of flocks shall we mourn?
